key_insight: Reasoning structure, not just surface wording, provides a more robust signal for attributing text to LLM authors.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests a practical defense for AI text forensics by using reasoning graphs and graph neural networks to improve robustness against paraphrasing and model updates.
method: Extract reasoning graphs from generated texts using an argument mining pipeline.
Train a graph neural network on the extracted reasoning structures.
Compare against a Longformer baseline for authorship attribution.
evidence_signal: The approach improves attribution by up to 27 percentage points under paraphrasing/backtranslation attacks and by 19 percentage points on texts from unseen model versions.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable argument-mining and graph extraction, which may introduce errors or reduce transferability across domains and languages.
paper_title: Show Me How You Reason and I'll Tell You Who You Are: Reasoning Graphs for Robust LLM Authorship Attribution
